meta.title: ComptaZen — Do the job first. Then automate it.
meta.description: ComptaZen embeds as your accounting technician, does the actual work, then builds and hands off the system that replaces it — fixed price, no subscription, yours outright.

Home.h1: Thinking about hiring an accounting technician?
Home.sub: Before the job posting, the ramp-up, and the recurring salary — there's another way in. I join your business and do the work myself, then build the system that keeps doing it after I leave.
Home.problem: Right now, someone in your business is either doing this by hand at 11pm before month-end close — or you're about to write a job posting for the person who will.
Home.problemHighlight: There's a third option, and it starts with someone who's actually done the job, not just automated it.
Home.servicesIntro: Each layer is sold on its own — start wherever makes sense for your business.
Home.whyBody: ComptaZen is new — there's no long client roster yet, and it's worth saying that plainly rather than padding this page with vague claims. What there is: a real, hands-on background as both an accounting technician and a software developer trained at 42 Québec, and automation work I've already shipped — a document-processing pipeline built end-to-end — before ComptaZen existed. When this site says “I do the job myself before I automate it,” it isn't a sales angle — it's my own career, in reverse order. Early clients get founder-level focus that gets harder to come by once the calendar fills up.
Home.finalCtaSub: 30 minutes. No pitch deck. Just what's eating your time and whether we're a fit.

work.name: Work
work.teaser: I embed as your accounting technician, hourly, for 2–4 months. The same work a hire in that seat would do.
work.problem: You need someone to actually do the accounting technician job — reconciliation, AP, filings, whatever the role covers — without committing to a full-time hire, the ramp-up, or the recurring salary before you know if it's the right fit.
work.build: I join your business as your accounting technician, hourly, for 2–4 months. The same day-to-day tasks a hire in that seat would handle.
work.outcome: The work gets done properly, by someone who understands both the accounting and what's worth automating — and you see exactly how the engagement runs before committing to anything bigger.

automation.name: Automation
automation.teaser: Once I've done it by hand, I automate what's repeatable. Fixed price, quoted only after Work — never before.
automation.problem: Doing the work by hand forever doesn't make sense once it's understood firsthand — but generic automation, built by someone who's never actually done the job, tends to miss the real exceptions.
automation.build: Automation scoped to exactly what Work uncovered — anything from a single workflow (invoicing, reconciliation, AR follow-up, GST/QST filing prep) up to the full role. Fixed price, quoted after Work, signed as its own contract.
automation.outcome: The repeatable share of the job runs on its own. No manual entry, no chasing, no re-keying numbers between systems.

judgment.name: Judgment
judgment.teaser: An AI layer that gives anomalies and exceptions a first pass. Standard (cloud) or Sovereign (self-hosted, fine-tuned). You always make the final call.
judgment.problem: Automation handles the repeatable work, but every accounting function has a layer that isn't pure data entry — anomalies, exceptions, first-pass audit prep — and that layer usually still eats hours every month.
judgment.build: An AI layer trained on your actual processes that gives exceptions and anomalies a first pass, and only surfaces what genuinely needs a decision. Available cloud-hosted (Standard) or fully self-hosted and fine-tuned for data-sensitive or regulated needs (Sovereign).
judgment.outcome: Less time spent scanning every line to find the two that matter. You still make every final call — the system just does the first read.

support-custom.name: Support & Custom
support-custom.teaser: Prepaid hours for anything after handoff. No subscription. First week free.
support-custom.problem: Systems need adjusting — a new tax rule, a new vendor, growth past what was originally scoped. And sometimes what's needed doesn't fit neatly into Work, Automation, or Judgment at all.
support-custom.build: Prepaid support hours for adjustments and anything post-handoff, or a scoped custom project for one-off requests that don't fit the ladder.
support-custom.outcome: Nothing breaks silently, and nothing outside the three layers gets turned away — it just gets its own quote.
support-custom.price: $120/hour, prepaid blocks · first week after handoff free

invoice-ap-automation.name: Invoice & AP Automation
invoice-ap-automation.problem: Someone on your team is manually entering invoice data, chasing approvals over email or Slack, then re-entering the same numbers into your accounting software.
invoice-ap-automation.build: Automated invoice capture and data extraction, an approval routing workflow that matches how your business actually approves spend, and a direct sync into QuickBooks, Xero, Zoho, or whatever you already run.
invoice-ap-automation.outcome: No manual entry. No duplicate payments. An AP process that runs in the background instead of eating an afternoon every week.

bank-reconciliation-automation.name: Bank & Reconciliation Automation
bank-reconciliation-automation.problem: Matching bank and credit card transactions against your books by hand is slow, error-prone, and the main reason month-end close drags on.
bank-reconciliation-automation.build: Automated transaction matching. Only genuine exceptions get flagged for a human — not every line.
bank-reconciliation-automation.outcome: Close goes from days to hours. Books that are actually current, not “current as of two weeks ago.”
bank-reconciliation-automation.note: Also available for accounting and bookkeeping firms managing this across dozens of client files — one automation, scaled across your whole book of business. Firm pricing: $2,000–$4,000 setup + $300–$800/month across your portfolio.

ar-collections-automation.name: AR & Collections Automation
ar-collections-automation.problem: Getting paid on time shouldn't depend on someone remembering to follow up. Manual chasing means inconsistent follow-through and cash sitting in other people's accounts longer than it should.
ar-collections-automation.build: Automated reminder sequences, escalating follow-ups, and a clear dashboard of what's outstanding and for how long.
ar-collections-automation.outcome: Faster collections, less owner time spent chasing invoices, a healthier cash position.

quebec-gst-qst-compliance.name: Quebec GST/QST Compliance Automation
quebec-gst-qst-compliance.problem: Remittance calculations, filing deadlines, and document retention for Revenu Québec's specific rules are a distinct headache from general bookkeeping — and almost nobody builds automation specifically for it.
quebec-gst-qst-compliance.build: Automated GST/QST calculation, filing-deadline reminders, and organized document archiving — built for Quebec's rules specifically, not adapted from a generic template.
quebec-gst-qst-compliance.outcome: Fewer scrambles before filing deadlines, a clean paper trail if Revenu Québec ever asks for one.
quebec-gst-qst-compliance.note: This automates calculation, tracking, and organization — not filing on your behalf, which involves separate authorized-representative rules we verify before offering as a bundled service.

data.label: Ownership
data.text: You own the system outright — not a subscription you're renting. If we ever part ways, it keeps running, and it's still yours.

cost.label: Cost
cost.text: No per-workflow SaaS subscriptions stacking up over time. Automation and Judgment are each built once, priced once.

fit.label: Fit
fit.text: Built around how your business actually approves spend and closes books — because I did the work myself before automating any of it.

audit.label: Audit
audit.text: One system to audit, not five vendors' worth of integrations, access logs, and data-sharing agreements.

AboutPage.founderBio: Hafid Saadi is an accounting technician and a software developer, trained in software engineering at 42 Québec. That combination is the reason ComptaZen exists: almost every small business's back office has the same gap — real work still done by hand that software should be doing instead — and almost nobody trying to fix it has actually done the work themselves first.
AboutPage.approachBody: Every engagement starts the same way: the job gets done by hand before anything gets automated. Only once it's actually been done does the system get scoped and built — yours outright, nothing glued together from third-party no-code platforms, nothing routing your financial data through tools you don't control.
AboutPage.headedBody: ComptaZen is deliberately starting with one thing: accounting operations for Quebec SMEs, done by someone who's actually done the job. The same method — do it, then build it — extends naturally to the judgment layer next: AI trained on real processes, not theoretical ones.

meta.title: Privacy Policy — ComptaZen
meta.description: How ComptaZen collects, uses, and protects your personal information.

sections.title: Who we are
sections.body: ComptaZen is a Quebec-based accounting process diagnostics and automation practice. For any question about this policy or your personal information, contact us at info@comptazen.digital.

sections.title: What we collect
sections.body: Our contact form on comptazen.digital collects: your name, your business name, your email address, and whatever you write in the “what's the most painful process” field. We don't collect anything else through this form, and we don't use tracking cookies or analytics scripts on this site.

sections.title: Why we collect it
sections.body: We use this information for exactly one purpose: to respond to your inquiry and, if you choose to proceed, to schedule and prepare for a discovery call. We do not use it for marketing, we do not sell it, and we do not share it with anyone except the service provider described below, strictly to deliver your message to us.

sections.title: Your consent
sections.body: By checking the box on the contact form before submitting, you consent to us collecting and using your information for the purpose described above. You can withdraw that consent at any time by emailing info@comptazen.digital — we'll stop using your information and delete it, except where we're legally required to keep records.

sections.title: Where your information goes
sections.body: When you submit the form, your information is sent directly to our CRM (Zoho CRM) through a serverless function, and stored on Zoho's systems rather than on servers we control. Zoho acts as a service provider for us in this respect. As with any service provider located outside Quebec, this transfer requires appropriate contractual safeguards to be in place — Zoho offers a data processing agreement for business accounts, which we're putting in order as part of setting this up.

sections.title: How long we keep it
sections.body: We keep contact form submissions for as long as they're relevant to an active or potential engagement, and delete them once that's no longer the case — in practice, no longer than 24 months after our last contact with you, unless you ask us to delete it sooner or we're required to retain it longer for legal reasons.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: Under Quebec's Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, you can ask us, at no cost, to: see what personal information we hold about you; correct it if it's inaccurate or incomplete; or delete it. Email info@comptazen.digital and we'll respond within 30 days.

sections.title: Security
sections.body: We take reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect your information against loss, unauthorized access, and disclosure. No system is perfectly secure, and we can't guarantee absolute security.

sections.title: If something goes wrong
sections.body: If we become aware of a confidentiality incident involving your personal information that presents a risk of serious injury, we'll notify you and the Commission d'accès à l'information as required by law.

sections.title: Complaints
sections.body: If you're unsatisfied with how we've handled your personal information, you can contact us directly at info@comptazen.digital, or file a complaint with Quebec's Commission d'accès à l'information (cai.gouv.qc.ca).

sections.title: Changes to this policy
sections.body: We'll update this page if how we handle your information changes, and update the date above.
